Not very customer-friendly (12-08-2018):
We had a reservation for 11 people yesterday (at 6:00 PM) and were only able to choose from a very limited menu.
Several of our group couldn't make a choice, so we asked about other options.
After consulting with the chef, we were allowed to choose from the menu as an exception, but were told it might take a very long time because everything was taken and the kitchen was very busy.
The staff was probably irritated because no one was around to take our drinks orders.
Because we had to wait so long for our main course, we looked around a bit.
Besides our group, there were four other people eating in the restaurant, and four tables outside were occupied.
We wondered what the staff meant by "everything was taken," and why the kitchen was so busy.
For years, we've ended our family day with dinner at a restaurant in the Kempen region.

A nice site definitely aimed at young Dutch families, in a great location, with some fantastic man-made beaches, petting zoo, swimming lakes, lots of kids activities, and great bike routes, but damage to the caravan due to lots of children constantly hitting it whilst playing football against it every day kind of spoilt it for us!

In fairness the site does tell guests that there are no ball games in pitched areas, and there are places specifically for kids to play football, and ride bikes etc, but not many took advantage of this, and the site does not enforce its rules, so your on your own dealing with lots of kids and parents that don’t seem to care or take notice of what their kids are doing.
The paid for WiFi hardly ever works, despite a great WiFi signal, so I’m posting this via my expensive 4G roaming service, so maybe bring a book or two!

The toilet/shower facilities are not too bad, fairly clean most of the time, but pretty basic and just not enough considering just how many people are here, so it’s best to take your shower etc out of normal hours if you don’t want to stand and wait in line for a long time.
The pitches are very densely laid out, and very close together and are not large enough to have your car next to your caravan, so everyone has to park alongside the access roads within the site.

There are not as many places to park as there are pitches, so don’t expect to be able to park close by after you have setup, the parking places are also not very large, and if you have a larger car, ie something large enough to tow a decent sized caravan, then don’t be surprised by any damage that could be done.

This park claims no responsibility to any damage to your property whatsoever, so if unsupervised children playing football break your caravan, or you get a dent in the side of your car, your totally on your own.

As non Dutch visitors here, I have to say that all of the staff were kind and helpful and very good speaking English, so that makes things a little better, but I don’t think I would recommend this site to foreign visitors, unless you have lots of kids and like it loud and fast!

SterrenStrand is a very nice little water park that combines an outdoor swimming lake with an indoor swimming complex.
The indoor area is split into two sections: a covered indoor beach and a more typical swimming complex.
The indoor beach is fully covered in sand and features a shallow, sand-bottomed cold-water lake with plenty of wooden play structures for kids.
The swimming complex includes a standard pool, two fun pools for babies and young children, a bubble pool, and a single water slide.
Next to the indoor beach, there is a covered terrace with plenty of tables where you can eat.
Bringing your own food and drinks is allowed, and there is also a bar offering various dishes, snacks, and drinks.
Beneath the terrace is an underground maze for kids, and nearby there is a small sand playground.
Lockers are available with a €1 coin.
Their yearly membership can be a great deal if you plan multiple visits.
However, its value is undermined by the fact that it is unusable during several periods of the year, including Dutch school holidays and most notably from early July to the end of August.
While it is a really fun spot for children, the price feels high for what is offered, especially compared to other water parks.
There is only one water slide (and its red/green light system was not working), limited options for older kids, and several wooden play features on the indoor beach have been broken for years.
Lifeguard supervision could also be improved, as teenagers sometimes play too roughly in the baby and bubble pools.
We did not try the outdoor swimming lake, so we cannot comment on that.
Overall, though, it is a great place for younger kids to enjoy.

Met gierende banden en eerder vertrokken

Na eerdere jaren op uitstekende campings gestaan te hebben zoals De Paal, Beerze Bulten, De Bongerd en de De Krim werd ons Ter Spegelt aangeraden.
Op het eerste oog een goed uitgeruste camping en dus een jaar van tevoren geboekt.
Het werd een campingplaats met privesanitair voor 2 weken voor een bedrag van 2000 euro.
Wifi voor de kinderen was voor dat aanzienlijke bedrag nog niet inbegrepen, dus dat diende dan nog aangeschaft te worden voor 44 euro voor twee weken en beperkt tot slechts 4 apparaten.
Privesanitair bleek op onze plaats behoorlijk gedateerd, alhoewel dat op andere plaatsen gemoderniseerd leek.
Bij aankomst leek nog niets mis, maar tijdens de eerste nacht werden we wakker gehouden door roepende en scheldende buren tot ver na middernacht, terwijl stilte is geboden na 23:00.
Toen de overlast de dagen erna aanhield hebben we tot 4x toe de nachtwaker gebeld die dan langskwam en er of iets van zei, of dat het net rustig was op dat moment (en erna weer begon).
We zijn vervolgens ook 3x bij de receptie geweest om de meldingen te herhalen en te vragen om actie, aangezien onze kinderen en wijzelf door de overlast niet in slaap konden komen.
Dit tastte ons vakantiegevoel terdege aan.
Bij de laatste keer bij de receptie werd toegezegd de overlastbrengers te benaderen.
Kort erna werden we gebeld met de reactie: de buren ontkenden luidruchting te zijn (wij van WC Eend) en de omringende buren hadden niets gehoord.
Detail: die omliggende buren waren allemaal net de dag ervoor aangekomen.

Voor wat betreft de empathie voor de overlast vanuit Ter Spegelt werd ons en passant daarbij verteld dat we teveel pop-up tentjes voor de kinderen hadden staan en dat die of weggehaald moesten worden of dat we bij moesten betalen.
Toen we vroegen of dat morgen kon ivm de regen werd dat afgewezen en kwam er een uur later iemand langs om te controleren of die al opgeruimd werden.
We hebben al jaren met plezier gecampeerd bij gerenommeerde campings in NL, maar Ter Spegelt hoort in dat rijtje echt niet thuis.
De campingsregels worden links en rechts overtreden, waarbij er zeer selectief ingegrepen wordt.

The private sanitary facilities at our pitch turned out to be quite dated, although they seemed to have been modernized at other sites.
Upon arrival, nothing seemed amiss, but during the first night, we were kept awake by neighbors shouting and cursing until well after midnight, even though silence is required after 11:00 PM.

When the disturbance continued in the following days, we called the night watchman four times, who would come by and either report something, or say it was quiet at that moment (and then start again).
We subsequently went to reception three times to reiterate the reports and request action, as our children and we couldn't sleep because of the disturbance.
This seriously affected our holiday spirit.
The last time we went to reception, they promised to contact the nuisance-causing guests.
Shortly afterward, we received a call with the following response: the neighbors denied being noisy (we, from WC Eend), and the surrounding neighbors hadn't heard anything.
The detail: those surrounding neighbors had all arrived the day before.

Regarding the empathy for the disturbance from Ter Spegelt, we were told in passing that we had too many pop-up tents for the children and that they either had to be removed or we would have to pay extra.
When we asked if that could be done tomorrow due to the rain, they refused, and an hour later someone came by to check if they had already been removed.
We've enjoyed camping at reputable campsites in the Netherlands for years, but Ter Spegelt definitely doesn't belong on that list.
The campsite rules are being broken left and right, and enforcement is very selective.
It's an expensive campsite, and additional costs for activities and Wi-Fi have to be factored in.
We're not the usual complainers, but we've never experienced anything like this before.
The one star is for the customer service of the reception staff, who are very dismissive.

I've been camping for 20 years, both in motorhomes and caravans.
So the experience itself isn't new to me, but this particular experience certainly was.

There were three of us:

-2 adults
-1 child (5 years old)

I specifically booked a chalet for 6 people to have enough space, but that was a mistake.
The double bed was somewhere between 120/140 and 190/200 cm, completely unsuitable for two adults (178 cm and 180 cm tall).
With outside temperatures of 32 degrees Celsius and everything closed up inside, it was easily 40 degrees (even though we knew guests were coming).
So, for a double bed advertised as being at least 160 cm wide, I expect it to be at least 160 cm wide.
Luckily, we had three bedrooms.
My husband moved into the room with the bunk beds, but they had equally odd dimensions, about 175-180 cm long, which was too short for me, the mother, at 180 cm.
Even my husband kept bumping his head or feet against the walls while sleeping.
In the third bedroom, our child slept at 114 cm.
Thankfully, the bed fit without any problems (since our child lay sideways across the double bed, leaving only a hand's width of space, we could estimate that the double bed was at most 140 cm wide).
The nights were very unrefreshing due to the overall situation and the poor mattresses, where you could feel every single spring.
The cleanliness also left much to be desired.
All the upholstery, whether the chairs, the sofa, or the garden furniture, was covered in stains and some even had food residue on it – simply disgusting.
We decided to just sit with towels and mention it upon departure because these stains (see photo) couldn't be easily removed.
A wet vacuum and deep cleaning would be necessary.
I would definitely wash the dishes and cutlery before using them.
The kettle was unusable (see photo).
I really wonder what the €50 final cleaning fee is for.
You have to take the rubbish to the main station yourself, make and strip the beds yourself, sweep, and do all the dishes.
Washing and sweeping is fine, but making the beds after having to do it yourself and then paying another €24 per set... Well, okay.
Furthermore, the floor was very uneven and creaked more than in any campervan I've ever vacationed in.
The walls are so thin that you can HEAR and FEEL your neighbors' footsteps at night!
We left a day early.
Because of the sweeping, stripping beds, taking out the trash, etc., we found it more pleasant to leave at midday with our child, instead of having to finish everything by 10:00 AM at the latest!
Upon departure, they asked if everything was okay.
I pointed out the issues.
Regarding the beds, they said they were a normal size.
When I suggested noting this on the website, they told me they could just call ahead and ask.
When I mentioned the soiled chairs, cushions, and furniture, they simply said, "No, no, they're clean.
You just can't see it because the stains are old and won't come out."
I then suggested that they could replace them or deep clean them, as it made a bad impression and simply looked dirty to the guests.
All I got was a shrug.
